[spoiler=War post]Growlers maintain their jamming of the Dutch jets. Pushing the Dutch to limit their data sources allows the HAF to maintain an information advantage. Fifth generation HAF jets linked to their AWACS and CCAs maintain a constant air contest against the Dutch. Firing off their radar guided Meteor BVRAAMs at before visual range towards the Dutch jets, the HAF and their CCAs maintain a constant pursuit. However, the HAF would also focus on permanently grounding the Dutch jets by destroying the base infrastructure required to fly the aircraft consistently. Using FAMMs and Tomahawk cruise missiles against a primarily passive anti-air system with worse off fire control, the HAF targets fuel sources, runways, arms depots, jets at their bases and maintenance. All designed to make it extremely difficult to maintain a constant air presence and ultimately kill the Dutch ability to fly. 

Despite the switch to DSSS and FHSS the Growlers would be able to maintain constant jamming of wireless communications. Barrage jamming utilizing HAF Compass Calls would work to overwhelm the entire range of frequencies used by the DSSS. The Growlers systems quickly track the frequency hopping systems as well. Taking into account dwell times, hop rates, bandwidth per hop and other factors the aircraft move to quickly predict where to jam. Additionally reactive jamming through tracking hops would be used to constantly suppress and degrade the Dutch ability to communicate. Pattern recognition of specific Dutch equipment uses of pulse repetition, modulation schemes and bandwidth patterns as well as secondary verification through electro-optical sensors and synthetic aperture radar allow the HDF to disregard decoys. The Dutch use of bursts to communicate wouldnt be able to slip past the HAF systems. Wideband continuous monitoring which allows the HDF to listen into a swath of a spectrum at once allows the HDF to pick up on small bursts no matter when or where they occur. The FOX-3 fire and forget missiles using onboard radar tracking continue towards their targets, disregarding the F-14 flare countermeasures completely. The JA-35 and J-22s of the Republik utilize their flat nozzles which spread out hot gases and internal weapons bays to minimize their IR signatures. At the same time the aircraft stay high and continuously utilize their CCAs to contest air superiority against the 4.5th generation jets. 

For the small area denial bubbles the HAF quickly works to break them. For those using active tracking, the JA-35s use MALD drones which mimic the signature of real aircraft to bait them into firing. Then the jets pursue a ruthless campaign of reactive SEAD. Using AGM-88ER anti-radiation missiles to fire well out of the AAA and SAM ranges at 150+ km, the JA-35s work to permanently break the remaining stores of credible air defense in Dutch territory. For passive SAMs the CCAs continue their bombing runs as they dont offer credible fire control capabilities against the UCAVs. MWS Harpy drones are used against the remaining pieces of the Dutch fleet. Sent in the thousands the fire and forget autonomous drones work towards exhausting the rest of the Dutch air defenses onboard. Finally, the JA-35s fire off their LRASM missiles towards the remaining ships. Using their sea-skimming capabilities, low radar cross section and autonomous tracking abilities the missiles close quickly with their Dutch targets. 

The beginning of the Dutch effort to rearm their forces with new radios, SAMs as well as standard supplies of ammunition, fuel and food would be the target of the HDF war effort. Essentially the HDF would move to cripple the Dutch logistical capability and therefore cripple the Dutch war effort. For fuel, with the Republik blockade already blocking off all oil imports into the country and with no native oil supplies to speak of in the Dutch State, the HAF would continue to hit remaining fuel supplies. Despite decentralization the fuel would still have infrastructure prerequisites for storing oil. Steel drums, fuel bladders, IBCs and the such that would be required to host credible armor and other energy intensive operations would be clearly visible to saturated aperture radar even if hidden under camouflage. UCAVs armed with 500 and 2,000-lb JDAMs are used to constantly assault Dutch fuel stores to cut off fuel sources for the Dutch military. MWS Harpy loitering munitions are used as well to attack both the fuel stores themselves but also used to autonomously target transport systems for the fuel as they move towards the frontlines. On transportation the UCAVs are used to strike highways and railroads used for military purposes. Using GBU-31, 2,000-lb JDAMs the Republik works to strike critical military transport infrastructure at as many points as possible while maximizing damage to make repairs near impossible. Additionally, FAMMs are used to continuously strike the Dutch electrical grid to cut off the distribution of energy towards critical equipment such as SAMs, command centers and radar installations. Using B-25EX stealth bombers the HDF maintains its campaign by striking major manufacturing centers with JDAMs to cut off the industrial capacity required to produce weapons for the war effort. The cumulative goal of this campaign would be to cut off the electricity, fuel, weapons, ammunition and food required to field a modern military and push enemy forces towards capitulation. 

Using their DIRCM turrets the helicopters quickly use their active protection systems to fire lasers towards the missiles and misguide them. Flying outside of the range of the 30mm guns, the helicopters use their hellfire missiles to try to suppress the remaining defenses. The CAS aircraft are engaged by the fleet's air defense systems long before they can arrive. SM-3 missiles fire off from the Hochdeutsche fleet to intercept the Fokkers long before they can arrive to the fight. MICLIC mine clearing vehicles are used to rapidly clear a breach and allow the newly arriving Hochdeutsche Armee heavy armor to move through. With rockets pulling long explosive lines across minefields to detonate mines and allow the Republik forces through the process is repeated and allows the combined ground forces to break through relatively quickly. The APS systems onboard the Republik IFVs and MBTs as well as ERA largely protect the vehicles from significant damage while allowing them to quickly fire back. 

With the Hochdeutsche Armee landing in the country, the ground force of 70,000 moves to rapidly capture the Dutch capital advancing with heavy air support.[/spoiler]

[b]January 24, 2028: Diplomacy with the West[/b]

Wuloosya and Yzakastan for the past thirty years have had cordial and blooming relations. Our oil has helped power their cities, their ships, their people, and has tied us closely together. Gentlemen, I implore you to pass the special resolution on the gift that the shah has proposed we give to the newly elected President Julian, thundered prelate Cahit in the echoing Chamber of the Peoples, which at the moment was only half full.

Mild applause filled the chamber as Cahit lowered himself via the wheelchair elevator to the floor of the chamber, shaking the hands of some over-enthusiastic interns. 

As one of his assistants took the handlebars of the wheelchair and wheeled him up the sloping floor of the chamber, he paused to chat with one of the members, a member of the revolutionary party who was kowtowing before him, I will get my members to vote on this resolution, please sir, let me kiss your ring, said the figure.

Of course my child, replied Cahit, presenting the ring which sat upon the sausages which were his fingers, the member gingerly kissed it, blessed Cahit in arabic, and then moved on quickly.

After a gaggle with the press, Cahit finally managed to arrive at the audience chambers of the Hall of the National Unity Congress, where the shah waited, dressed in a simple suit and tie.
Your honour, chortled Cahit, waving his assistant away and out of the room.

Alparslan, it is once again an honour to see you, replied the Shah warmly, Now I wanted to first congratulate you on your speech, I am sure well get the votes to procure that jet for the president, replied the Shah with a kind smile.

Of course! chuckled Cahit, patting his belly, A jumbo-jet nonetheless, for our allies in the West, 

Yes, replied the Shah, frowning slightly, Though I would wonder, the cost of it, is it too much? 

My dear Shah, nothing is too much for the president of Wuloosya, the arrangement is simple, we give them oil, they share weapons, it is a wonderful arrangement, clapped Cahit, putting his hands together. 

Yes, but the debt, and the fact we are using a special resolution, it seems a bit backwards, replied the shah, his eyebrows creasing. 

The cost will be covered by our oil sales, replied Cahit, And, with your trip to them soon, well, the optics, they are beautiful! 

I spoke with the Senate Appropriations Committee today, they said that the votes are present, but they are like me, they worry of the cost, replied the Shah.

Ah, the SAC is always flustered about money, do not listen to them, replied Cahit with a dismissive wave of his hand, Come now, I have the draft of the announcement that will be presented to the state department, replied Cahit, pulling a tablet out of his briefcase to show the text to the shah.

Its very simple, remarked the shah.

Of course, the Wuloosyan government doesnt like fluff, replied Cahit.

Very well, I approve of its being sent to the state department, the plane is mentioned right? asked the Shah.

Yes, it is mentioned,

Very well then, send it, said the Shah.

-----

Al-Upran lies back on his overly fanciful chair, tied down within a medium-sized compartment. He takes another puff of his cigarette. The room grows further choked in his addiction; he breathes it in, coughing. The smog exhales with him as the door is opened, his left hand dashes for his sidearm in fear. But his fear was in folly, just a younger brother come to inform him of the imminent docking. Al-Upran crushes out his cig and stands up. He points vaguely to the right and barks orders. 

[b]"Go get the cash reserve, park us in the least busy dock and prepare to bribe the docking officials. Call Hamza, get his ass and his new compadre's behind to get us a rendezvous point as soon as the bribe leaves your grubby hands."[/b]

The younger brother nodded, fear and awe mixed in his face as he followed Al-Upran's orders. Retrieving a bundle of cash from a very small safe, he takes his leave of the vessel and puts on as brave a face as he can muster. His sidearm nuzzles his ribs, tucked under a coat slightly too big for him. The night sky without stars disappoints him, but he presses on, making his way past the rows of shipping containers full of guns, opium and rotting potatoes.

He climbs down and steps onto the dockyard, inspection officers lazily milling about during their impromptu nightshift. The half-asleep officer accepts the bribe, partially out of moral bankruptcy and partly out of thinking it was a dream. The officer returns to his cosy office chair and passes out. 

In the quiet of the night, the family takes over for the dock workers and begins the rapid transport of four or so containers brought to show their might to their new potential overlord. They make their way to whatever rendezvous point Hamza decided to set. They arrive shortly after the B4L's, in the shroud of a cold Brunswick night.
